content.value_statement: Advanced TypeScript types can become hard to design, review, and maintain. This skill gives structured guidance for safer generics, utilities, APIs, and state models.
actual_capabilities: Explains generics, constraints, conditional types, mapped types, and template literal types.
Provides patterns for typed event emitters, API clients, builders, and form validation.
Guides utility types, type guards, assertion functions, and infer-based extraction.
Highlights strict mode, type tests, and performance limits for complex type logic.
Helps migrate JavaScript patterns toward safer TypeScript designs.
limitations: Does not run TypeScript compilers or verify project-specific build output by itself.
Does not replace runtime validation for external data or API responses.
Examples are educational and may need adaptation for framework conventions.
Very complex recursive types can still reduce compiler performance.

use_cases.title: Design a Type-Safe Library
use_cases.description: Create public utility types and generic APIs with clearer constraints and safer inference.

use_cases.title: Model API Contracts
use_cases.description: Represent routes, methods, request bodies, parameters, and responses with compile-time checks.

use_cases.title: Improve Migration Safety
use_cases.description: Replace loose JavaScript patterns with strict TypeScript types during incremental migration work.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Type Concept
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how TypeScript conditional types work for my use case. Use simple examples and list common edge cases.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Type Utility
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this TypeScript utility type and suggest a clearer version with safer constraints and better inference.

prompt_templates.title: Design Typed APIs
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a type-safe API client model for these routes, methods, request inputs, and response shapes.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Type Complexity
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these advanced TypeScript types for readability, compile performance, recursion depth, and safer alternatives.

output_examples.input: Explain when to use mapped types for user settings.
output: The response contrasts mapped types with explicit object shapes.
It recommends mapped types for repeated property transformations.
It warns against hiding simple models behind complex abstractions.

output_examples.input: Design a type-safe API client for user routes.
output: The response defines how route names, methods, parameters, bodies, and responses should relate.
It identifies where runtime validation is still required.
It suggests type tests for public client behavior.

output_examples.input: Improve a recursive path type that slows the compiler.
output: The response highlights recursion depth and nested conditional type costs.
It recommends simpler boundaries and documented limits.
It suggests measuring compiler impact before wider adoption.

best_practices: Use strict compiler options before adding advanced type abstractions to a project.
Write type tests for reusable utilities and public API contracts.
Keep recursive and conditional types shallow enough for readable errors.
anti_patterns: Do not use any to bypass errors caused by unfinished type design.
Do not encode runtime validation only in TypeScript types.
Do not create deeply nested types when simple interfaces are clear.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps design and review advanced TypeScript types for safer application and library code.

faq.question: Can it review existing type utilities?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the utility goal, current type design, and any compiler errors or confusing inference results.

faq.question: Does it execute code or install packages?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Project verification remains the user's responsibility.

faq.question: Can it help with API client types?
faq.answer: Yes. It can model routes, methods, request inputs, parameters, and response types.

faq.question: Will it replace runtime validation?
faq.answer: No. Runtime validation is still needed for external data, user input, and API responses.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: Claude, Codex, and Claude Code can use this skill for TypeScript type guidance.
